newsitem.title: TURKEY: Accidental grenade blast kills 7 at Turk wedding.
newsitem.headline: Accidental grenade blast kills 7 at Turk wedding.

text.p: A hand grenade worn by a reveller at a wedding party in southeast Turkey exploded accidentally and seven people were killed and 50 were wounded by the blast and the ensuing panic, a police official said on Saturday.

"The explosion was caused when the pin of a hand grenade on a dancing village guard was pulled accidentally by the vest worn by another man dancing next to him," Vehbi Gokalp, police chief of the largely Kurdish Sirnak province, told Reuters.
Police detained 60 people, including the groom, on charges of negligence after the incident late on Friday in the town of Cizre, near the Iraqi border.
"Three people died immediately but the ensuing panic caused many of the casualties. Seven people were killed and 50 wounded," Gokalp said. Most of the casualties were women and children, he said.
Both the bride and groom were unhurt, police said.

Witnesses said village guards, members of a government-paid Kurdish militia against the separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), shot in the air to seek help from security forces after the explosion.

However, the regional governor, quoted by Anatolian news agency, said many of the injured were wounded by wild gunfire, apparently touched off by panic after the blast. Most of the wedding guests were heavily armed, the agency said.
Earlier security officials said the blast might have been the work of the PKK, which has targeted the village guards in its bloody insurgency for Kurdish self-rule.
The wounded were taken to hospitals in Cizre and the nearby administrative centre of Diyarbakir.

"The explosion occurred while some people were dancing and others watching them. The PKK might have done it because we are village guards," Idris Idim, a wounded guard taken to a hospital in Diyarbakir, told Reuters.

Idim said the wedding belonged to the Kulanc family, many of whose men became village guards during the 12-year-old fight against the PKK's war for independence or autonomy in southeast Turkey in which more than 26,000 people have died.
